thread:
incident-bot: CRIT: Dedicated pool-9 p99 latency SLO breach for streaming endpoints in us-east-1. Queue depth alarm > 150. Paging the oncall rota.

maya (oncall): confirming alert. I'm on it. Starting thread for triage and coordination.

maya (oncall): quick metrics: p95 jumped from ~180ms -> 520ms, p99 jumped from ~1.1s -> 6.4s. Stream stalls reported, chunk gaps ~3-8s. Dashboard: https://redwood.internal/dash/pools/pool-9?range=30m

raj (infra): checking scale activity. Autoscaler attempted a scale(+5) at 16:12:07 UTC. Several handshake failures show up in infra logs around 16:12:40. Error: "agent handshake failed: kv-sync not completed". New hosts provisioned but never marked ready.

liam (sre): paste the log excerpt? want to confirm if it's kv-sync or something else timing out.

raj (infra): pasted snippet:
```
2026-04-04T16:12:07Z autoscaler: scale request +5 pool-9
2026-04-04T16:12:42Z vm-982 infra-agent: instance created
2026-04-04T16:13:10Z warmup-probe[vm-982]: kv-sync timeout after 45s
2026-04-04T16:13:10Z infra-agent[vm-982]: handshake failed: not-ready
2026-04-04T16:13:20Z autoscaler: backoff, retry scheduled
```

sophia (eng-platform): same class of failure we've seen before. New runtime build on image v2.0.0 appears to increase kv-sync latency for long-prefix models. When warmup probe fails, node never joins serving and requests queue. Pool queue now at 161; serve rate unchanged.

maya (oncall): customer impact? any direct reports?

jordan (support): two customers opened tickets: NexaHealth (high-volume streaming for transcription) and FinFlow (low-volume). NexaHealth flagged production impact.

amelia (customer-success): I messaged NexaHealth CSM and told them we are triaging; requested permission to route them to a fallback while we mitigate. They want live status and a timeline.

liam (sre): propose immediate mitigations:
- shift streaming tokens for impacted customers to fallback pool-3 (compatible variant)
- throttle non-critical background routes to preserve capacity for streaming
- manual scale-up using last-known-good image (v1.9.6) and force warmup with extended timeout
- enable temporary kv-prefetch-bypass for streaming for 15m if warmup remains slow
I'll take throttling and metrics. @raj do manual scale/warmup. @sophia handle routing rule for NexaHealth.

raj (infra): executing manual actions now. Commands:
```
infractl scale --pool pool-9 --add-instances 6 --image redwood-runtime-v1.9.6 --instance-type stable-32g
infractl warmup --pool pool-9 --instances vm-983,vm-984 --override-timeout 120s
```

raj (infra): instances provisioned; warmup shows kv-sync progressing on vm-983/984. ETA ~70s. Autoscaler logs now show handshake success for those two. Queue depth trending down from 161 -> 48 over 2 min.

sophia (eng-platform): applied a targeted routing rule for NexaHealth tokens -> pool-3. change id route-20260404-09. This is scoped so only NexaHealth streaming tokens are affected.

incident-bot: NOTE: routing change applied (route-20260404-09).

jordan (support): NexaHealth confirms streams smoothing out after routing. FinFlow still seeing intermittent 2-3s gaps but not total stalls.

liam (sre): current telemetry: p95 ~210ms, p99 ~950ms. Streaming stalls largely mitigated but tail spikes still appear for some long-prefix requests. Suspect some requests still landing on nodes that had partial kv-cache leading to re-fetch in-path.

sophia (eng-platform): secondary mitigation: enable temporary in-flight fallback to non-prefetch path for streaming endpoints for 10m. This will serve without full prefix cache, trading small quality regression for latency. Anyone object?

maya (oncall): ok for affected customers only. Put a rollback timer for 10m.

sophia (eng-platform): toggled pref-bypass for streaming (change id pref-20260404-02). Monitoring traces.

jordan (support): NexaHealth: "Much better, thank you." FinFlow: latency back within SLA.

liam (sre): after mitigations p99 stable below SLO at ~780ms, p95 ~190ms, queue depth ~12. We'll keep monitoring for 30m.

maya (oncall): root cause hypothesis: image v2.0.0 increased kv-sync/warmup times for certain model families; autoscaler did not fallback to older instance type leading to capacity gap -> request queuing -> p99 spike.

maya (oncall): follow-ups and owners:
- INF-4901: infra to rollback or validate v2.0.0 and run systematic warmup benchmarks (owner: raj (infra))
- PLAT-3380: autoscaler to detect repeated handshake failures and automatically try alternate image/host-type (owner: sophia (eng-platform))
- RUN-7222: SRE update runbook: add warmup-failure detection steps and quick mitigation commands used here (owner: liam (sre))
- CS-211: customer comms and postmortem for NexaHealth (owner: amelia (customer-success))

raj (infra): scheduled canary validation of v2.0.0 tomorrow morning; temporary revert applied to autoscaler config for pool-9. Filed INF-4901.

sophia (eng-platform): will implement handshake-failure circuit: if >3 failures in 10m, autoscaler will try fallback image/host. Filed PLAT-3380.

liam (sre): updating alerting: add warmup-failure rate alert and a separate slack page for autoscaler handshake spike. Also will add automated dashboard that surfaces kv-sync durations by image.

amelia (customer-success): NexaHealth accepted a postmortem + goodwill credit. I'll coordinate the writeup with ops owners.

maya (oncall): stability looks good for 25m. I'll handoff to night oncall libby for overnight watch and to track postmortem.

incident-bot: RESOLVED: Pool-9 queue depth and SLOs restored. Incident duration ~37m.

libby (oncall-night): acknowledged. I'll pick up the postmortem review in the AM and watch the warmup metrics overnight.

maya (oncall): checklist before close:
- [x] manual scale + warmup done with v1.9.6
- [x] targeted routing for NexaHealth applied
- [x] pref-bypass enabled for impacted streaming, then rolled back
- [x] customers notified and CSM engaged
- [ ] postmortem draft (owner: maya)
- [ ] infra image validation canary (owner: raj)
- [ ] autoscaler failure fallback feature (owner: sophia)
- [ ] runbook updates (owner: liam)

maya (oncall): good job team. Closing thread after handoff. Please add any further notes here.

libby (oncall-night): noted. Monitoring.

maya (oncall): thread closed. Thanks :thumbsup:
